update.headline: Risk appetite improved despite firmer inflation prints, with technology still leading while rates and dollar pressure remain the main cross-asset constraint.
update.economy: Inflation data leaned firmer at the headline level: CPI y/y rose to 3.71% from 3.54%, a 0.17 pp increase, and CPI m/m rose to 0.4% from 0.07%, a 0.33 pp increase. PCE y/y rose to 3.42% from 3.36%, and PCE m/m rose to 0.31% from 0.05%. Core inflation was mixed: Core CPI y/y eased to 2.76% from 2.79%, but Core CPI m/m rose to 0.29% from 0.22%; Core PCE y/y rose to 3.01% from 2.98%, and Core PCE m/m rose to 0.25% from 0.13%. The labor signal softened: unemployment rose to 4.2% from 4.1%, while payrolls y/y slowed to 0.31% from 0.34%. Industrial production improved to 1.42% y/y from 1.13%, keeping the growth backdrop from looking broadly weak. Consensus and surprise data are unavailable in the snapshot.
update.asset_classes: Equities traded risk-on: SPY rose 0.81% on the day, QQQ rose 0.75%, and XLK rose 0.91%, with QQQ up 6.08% over 1 month and XLK up 8.39%. That keeps the market aligned with the narrow technology leadership theme. Cyclicals were mixed: XLE rose 0.72% on the day and 3.85% over 1 week, but only 0.36% over 1 month; XLF rose 0.5% on the day but remains down -6.47% over 1 month. Rates stayed a headwind: DGS2 rose 5.0 bp on the day and 44.0 bp over 1 month, while DGS10 rose 4.0 bp on the day and 49.0 bp over 1 month. Duration proxies bounced on the day, with TLT up 0.57% and IEF up 0.37%, but the 1-month trend remains negative at -5.29% for TLT and -2.92% for IEF. Credit also bounced, with LQD up 0.47% and HYG up 0.4% on the day, but both remain negative over 1 month at -2.59% and -1.93%. Commodities were mixed: gold bounced, with GLD up 0.58% and GC_F up 0.97% on the day, but both remain down over 1 month at -6.15% and -6.24%; oil was soft, with USO down -0.45% and CL_F down -0.78% on the day. FX still shows a firmer-dollar backdrop over 1 month: EURUSD is down -3.0%, AUDUSD is down -3.06%, GBPUSD is down -1.78%, USDJPY is up 1.24%, and USDCAD is up 3.37%.
update.predictions_changed: No regime prediction changed. The growth model gate is unchanged, so the old and new outputs are identical and should be treated as no forecast change. The inflation model gate is also unchanged, so the old and new outputs are identical and should not be presented as a refit-driven forecast. No data gaps were listed. No model note was provided.

themes_touched.title: Narrow technology leadership versus cyclical weakness
themes_touched.text: Still active. The risk-on day was led by growth and technology rather than broad cyclicals: SPY rose 0.81%, QQQ rose 0.75%, and XLK rose 0.91%, while XLK is up 8.39% over 1 month versus XLF down -6.47%, XLY down -2.63%, XLI down -1.52%, and XLV down -1.91%. Energy is strong longer term, but its 1-month return is only 0.36%, so leadership is still concentrated in technology.

themes_touched.title: Duration pressure and stronger-dollar stress
themes_touched.text: Still active. Yields rose again, with DGS2 up 5.0 bp on the day and 44.0 bp over 1 month, and DGS10 up 4.0 bp on the day and 49.0 bp over 1 month. Duration-sensitive assets bounced on the day, but TLT is still down -5.29% over 1 month, IEF is down -2.92%, LQD is down -2.59%, and GLD is down -6.15%. The dollar backdrop also remains firm over 1 month, with EURUSD down -3.0%, AUDUSD down -3.06%, GBPUSD down -1.78%, and USDCAD up 3.37%.

sector_reads.text: Energy looks like a short-term flat patch inside a powerful long-term uptrend, not a reversal. XLE is up 3.85% over 1 week and 0.36% over 1 month, but up 15.63% over 3 months and 47.86% over 12 months, with 29.88 pp relative 12-month performance. The near-term lag versus SPY, shown by -1.31 pp relative 1-month performance, looks like consolidation while oil is soft, with CL_F down -3.01% over 1 month.

Financials remain a weak spot. XLF is up 0.26% over 1 week but down -6.47% over 1 month, with -8.14 pp relative 1-month performance. The long trend is range-bound, with a 2.39% 12-month return and -15.59 pp relative 12-month performance, so this looks like downside within a weak range rather than a clean pullback in an uptrend.

Industrials are in a short-term pullback within a fading longer uptrend. XLI is down -1.52% over 1 month and -4.33% over 3 months, with -3.19 pp relative 1-month performance, but remains up 12.76% over 12 months. Because the long label is uptrend, fading and relative 12-month performance is -5.22 pp, this still looks more like a pullback than a confirmed reversal, but trend quality is deteriorating.

Health care weakness is short-term and deepening, but the longer trend is still positive. XLV is down -1.87% over 1 week and -1.91% over 1 month, with -3.58 pp relative 1-month performance, yet it is up 15.25% over 6 months and 17.62% over 12 months. This looks like a pullback inside an uptrend rather than a reversal, though relative 12-month performance is slightly negative at -0.36 pp.

Technology remains the dominant leadership sector. XLK is up 4.25% over 1 week, 8.39% over 1 month, 47.89% over 6 months, and 43.16% over 12 months, with 6.72 pp relative 1-month performance and 25.18 pp relative 12-month performance. There is no short-versus-long divergence here: the short trend is accelerating and the long trend remains an uptrend.

Consumer discretionary is bouncing short term but remains in a downtrend. XLY is up 2.29% over 1 week, yet down -2.63% over 1 month and -5.35% over 12 months, with -4.3 pp relative 1-month performance and -23.33 pp relative 12-month performance. This looks like an easing bounce within a broader downtrend, not a reversal.
